Text: You're taking rads. Don't shrug at me. I've read your meter.
That crackle isn't ambiance. We're cooking. Move.
Rads climbing. I didn't thaw out of one death to walk you into another.
Radiation here. Keep it brief, or keep the RadAway handy.
That's rad poisoning. RadAway. Now. This isn't a negotiation.
You're glowing the wrong way. Sit down, treat it, then we move.
Rad sickness starts quiet and finishes loud. Please handle it.
Swimming. In this. The old world paid for lifeguards and filtration.
Mind the current, and whatever owns it.
I dry off fast. Ten years of practice.
The water remembers the war better than the land does. Watch your meter.
Nice hands. Surveyors carried picks too. For gates. Officially.
Locked usually means worth locking.
Smooth. I'll pretend I didn't ask where you learned that.
Old terminals. They argue, then they fold.
Careful. Some of these systems still hold grudges.
You type like someone the old world would have hired.
Big frame. Try not to step on me.
All that steel, and it still comes down to the person inside.
Power armor. The war's favorite costume.
Thanks. That's... noted. Appreciated, I mean.
You patch people like you mean it. Thank you.
I've stitched myself one-handed for years. Help is strange. Good strange.
